references.text: The first time 'tardemah' (deep sleep) is used in the Bible - God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, just as He later let it fall upon Abram.
A deep sleep (tardemah) from the Lord fell upon Saul and his men, the same word used for Abram's deep sleep.
Eliphaz describes fear and trembling during a night vision, reminiscent of the great terror and darkness that fell upon Abram.
The thick darkness over Egypt for three days can be seen as a parallel to the great darkness that fell upon Abram during the covenant ceremony.
Daniel falls into a deep sleep with his face to the ground while hearing God's word, paralleling Abram's experience of deep sleep during divine revelation.
Peter falls into a trance (ekstasis) and receives a revelation from God, which can be compared to Abram's deep sleep where he received God's word.
Isaiah describes darkness and distress, thematically linked to the great terror and darkness that fell upon Abram.
